purpose: Independent fictional held-out set v2, written blind without access to the ranking implementation or earlier cases. Must not be edited or tuned to.
author: independent blind writer (no implementation access)

cases.name: quillmoor-original-launch-date
cases.query: what launch date did i first give for quillmoor, before we pushed it back?

records.text: Welcome back! Last time we wrapped up the Quillmoor pricing table. What's next on the list?
next is the launch itself. lets say march 14 for the quillmoor landing page go-live, copy's mostly done, design still WIP

March 14 for go-live gives you roughly three weeks. I'd suggest a design freeze around March 7 so there's a full week for QA, copy tweaks and the analytics setup. If design slips past the freeze, the launch date should move with it rather than squeezing QA.
design's slipping, Ines is out sick. push launch to march 28
Done. The Quillmoor launch moves from the original March 14 date to March 28, and the design freeze shifts to March 21.

Summary: Planned the Quillmoor landing page launch. Launch was first set for an early-March date, then pushed back two weeks to March 28 because of design delays (Ines out sick); design freeze moved to March 21.

cases.rationale: The user's own message at index 1 is where the original March 14 date was first set. The assistant's later restatement and the vaguer summary are only derived from it.

cases.name: ferncastle-current-rate-limit
cases.query: whats the ferncastle per-key rate limit set to now?

records.text: for the ferncastle public api lets cap it at 200 requests/min per key

A 200 req/min per-key cap is reasonable for a public API. I'd implement it as a token bucket keyed on the API key: capacity 200, refill 200 per 60s. Return 429 with a Retry-After header when the bucket is empty, and expose X-RateLimit-Remaining so clients can back off before they hit the wall. If internal services share the same keys you may want an allowlist.
hmm partners are already complaining. make that 500
Sure, 500/min per key. Do you want to allow short bursts above that, e.g. 2x for 10 seconds?
no bursts. and actually scratch 500, ops pushed back hard. go with 350 as the compromise
Understood. Separately, for the Ferncastle status dashboard, should the rate-limit chart show per-minute or per-hour buckets? Per-minute is noisier but matches how the limit is enforced.
per hour is fine, nobody looks at it anyway lol

cases.rationale: The user's correction to 350 replaces both 200 and 500. Later records talk about the rate-limit chart, not the value.

cases.name: brindlewick-database-choice-summary
cases.query: which db did we settle on for brindlewick in the end

records.text: Summary: Discussed storage for the Brindlewick inventory service. Compared Postgres, SQLite and a managed key-value store; user leaned toward the key-value store at first for cost, then decided on Postgres because the warehouse team needs relational reporting. SQLite kept only for local unit tests.
ok next, brindlewick CI keeps failing on the migrations step, maybe 1 in 4 runs

Intermittent migration failures usually mean the database container isn't accepting connections yet when the migrate job starts. Add a readiness check (poll in a loop with a timeout) before running migrations, and make sure the job doesn't share a database with parallel test shards.
yeah prob the db container racing. ok what about caching the sku lookups

For SKU lookups, an in-process LRU with a short TTL (say 60s) is probably enough for the read pattern you described. If you scale past a few instances, move to a shared cache so invalidations on price changes propagate.

cases.rationale: Only the summary records the final database decision (Postgres). The later records mention the database container and caching but never the choice.

cases.name: tallowmere-retry-count-short-edit
cases.query: how many retries does the tallowmere uploader do now

records.text: write me a retry wrapper for the tallowmere uploader. 5 retries, exponential backoff, python
nice. can u add logging for each attempt + jitter

Updated version: MAX_RETRIES stays at 5, and each failed attempt now logs 'upload retry {n}/5 after {delay:.1f}s' at WARNING level, with the exception type included. Jitter is full jitter: delay = random.uniform(0, BASE_DELAY * 2 ** attempt), which spreads retries out when lots of Tallowmere uploaders fail together. The final failure logs at ERROR with the total elapsed time before re-raising, so you can tell retry exhaustion apart from a single hard failure in the logs.
make it 9 instead
Will do. One thing to check: are Tallowmere uploads idempotent on the server side? With more retry attempts, a timeout that actually succeeded could create duplicate objects.

cases.rationale: The short edit 'make it 9 instead' changes the retry count. The long assistant replies that repeat 'retries' all still describe the old value of 5.

Got it. Owlbridge production port changed from 443 to 8443 behind the new load balancer; I'll treat that as the decided value. Does staging change too, or does it stay as is?

cases.name: marrowfield-onboarding-email-owner-paraphrase

Noted: Tomas owns the Marrowfield monthly newsletter and you own release notes.
oh and the welcome drip for new signups is Dessa's thing, she writes + schedules all of it
Great. For the onboarding emails, do you want a 3-step or 5-step sequence? Five steps lets you introduce integrations separately, but three tends to get better completion rates for small products.

Teal and coral on cream is a nice combo: teal reads trustworthy, coral feels appetizing. I'd keep coral for CTAs only so it doesn't overwhelm the menu screens.

cases.name: gristhollow-venue-by-elimination-summary
cases.query: which venue did we end up booking for the gristhollow offsite

records.text: gristhollow offsite: ~40 people, october, need a venue within 2h of the city

Three options that fit: Lakeside Lodge (2h15, gorgeous but a stretch on travel), Copperleaf Pavilion (central, but capacity is 30 seated), and Ashgrove Barn (1h40, sleeps 45, has a kitchen). Want me to compare prices?
lakeside is too far honestly, people will riot

Summary: Continued Gristhollow offsite venue discussion. Lakeside Lodge ruled out (travel time), Copperleaf Pavilion ruled out (too small for 40). By elimination the group went with Ashgrove Barn for the October offsite; deposit to be paid by Friday. Catering still open.
ok catering now. needs to be veggie friendly, a couple vegans too
Since the venue has its own kitchen, you could bring in a caterer who cooks on site. Fennel & Fig and Brass Spoon both do fully vegan menus; Fennel & Fig is cheaper for groups over 35.
fennel & fig. book em

cases.rationale: No user message ever explicitly picks Ashgrove Barn; the choice came by elimination, and only the summary states it. Index 1 lists every venue name but decides nothing, and index 6 books the caterer.

cases.name: lanternfell-thumbnail-cache-command
cases.query: what was the command to rebuild the lanternfell image preview cache

records.text: lanternfell's thumbnail cache is stale again, how do i nuke and regenerate it

Run `lf-cli cache purge --scope thumbs` and then `lf-cli cache warm --scope thumbs --concurrency 4`. Purge drops the stale entries; warm regenerates them from the originals so the first page loads aren't slow.
worked, thx. separately how do i clear the session store, ppl getting logged out weirdly
`lf-cli sessions flush --all` clears every session; add `--older-than 7d` if you only want to drop old ones. If logouts look random, check that all nodes share the same signing secret.
the secret thing was it lol. Rafaela had rotated it on one node
Classic. Worth adding a startup check that refuses to boot if a node's secret hash differs from the rest of the cluster.

cases.rationale: The query says 'image preview cache' and 'rebuild', meaning the thumbnail cache. The assistant reply at index 1 holds the actual purge/warm commands; index 3 is a command for a different store.
